bends.reason: This is the only recipe bend (1 · B1 · 7641b5). It is the long line between the main curved body and the narrow strip flange that carries two holes. Section (bend_01.png): the registered scan lies on the blue FORMED profile on both sides of the bend line. It follows both sheet faces through the kink at x=0, the second kink near x=-10 mm, the curve out to x=-40 mm and the flange end return at about x=+11 mm. I measured the pixels: the scan's segment directions are about +12 deg left of the line and -12 deg right of it, so the bend is roughly 24 deg. The orange NOT_FORMED profile is nearly straight across the line (left segment about -13 deg) and sits 3.7, 7, 11 and 17 mm above the scan at x=-8, -15, -25 and -38 mm. The scan follows none of it. Overlay views: in ISO, TOP, FRONT and SIDE the registered scan covers the whole B1 flange along its full length. Both flange holes show up in the scan where the CAD has them, and the flange's free edge meets the CAD edge with only a thin sliver of CAD surface showing. FRONT shows a visible crease in the scan exactly along the red line. Raw scan in its own frame, with no CAD: the FRONT view independently shows a separate flange facet meeting the sloped region at an angled crease, so the result does not depend on the registration. One limit: the angle comes from a single section, so I give it only as about 24 deg. The formed/not-formed call itself is unambiguous.
